chapter_seo_title: Han Li Conscripted for Mine Guard Duty – Mortal Stream Chapter 265
chapter_meta_description: Han Li is forcibly conscripted into a mine-guarding mission as the Six Demonic Sects invade Yue. He pivots his cultivation strategy to the Great Derivative Art and puppetry for survival.
og_title: A Change in Priorities – Conscription in the Mortal Stream
og_description: War comes to Yue. Han Li accepts a draft notice, reports the Yan Clan's betrayal, and immediately recalibrates his entire cultivation plan for survival.
twitter_title: Han Li's new plan: puppets over sword arts
twitter_description: Drafted into a mine guard mission, Han Li shelves the Azure Origin Sword Art and bets on the Great Derivative Art and puppets to survive the coming war.

lore_anchors.definition: An officially signed command from sect leaders, legally binding all sect disciples to temporary conscription; refusing it carries severe penalties.
A foundational mental cultivation technique from the Thousand Bamboo School; it strengthens divine sense and enables the Soul Divide technique for controlling multiple puppets.
A mid-grade formation that balances offensive and defensive capabilities; ideal for resource-constrained guard duties.
Han Li's primary cultivation technique; it only becomes competitive with peak demonic arts after reaching Core Formation.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Han Li accept the mobilization order so easily?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He has no real choice—refusing a legitimate order signed by all Seven Sect leaders would be a capital offense. His surface compliance masks a cold calculation of his odds.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the 'Great Derivative Art' and why does Han Li suddenly switch to it?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It is a divine-sense-strengthening technique that allows him to control multiple puppets at once. After his near-death duel with the Ghost Spirit Sect Young Lord, he realizes his current sword art is useless until Core Formation, so he pivots to puppetry for immediate combat power.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the 'leave request note' at the end?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It is a web novel author's honest, transparent apology for a slow update—a common cultural practice in Chinese serialization that acknowledges the reader-author relationship.
